details: The United States has reimposed a naval blockade on Iran, leading to significant uncertainty regarding energy flows through the Strait of Hormuz. Although an initial proposal for a 20% transit fee was later abandoned by President Trump for alternative investment deals with Gulf states, the escalated tensions, including reported attacks on tankers, caused Brent crude oil prices to climb to a one-month high. This situation forces cryptocurrency markets to recalibrate geopolitical risk, contributing to a "risk-off" sentiment.
title: US Reinstates Iran Naval Blockade, Oil Prices Jump on Hormuz Uncertainty

details: The European Central Bank (ECB) has chosen 36 payment service providers to participate in a 12-month pilot program for the digital euro, scheduled to commence in the latter half of 2027. This initiative is geared towards preparing for a potential launch by 2029, with the aim of mitigating the dominance of U.S. payment systems and dollar-backed stablecoins. Conversely, the U.S. has passed legislation that prevents the Federal Reserve from issuing a digital dollar until at least December 31, 2030, citing concerns over financial stability and individual privacy.
title: ECB Selects 36 Firms for Digital Euro Pilot as US Blocks Digital Dollar

details: A bipartisan bill introduced in the U.S. Senate seeks to impose tariffs of up to 100% on the top five nations purchasing Russian oil and gas, notably China and India. The legislation also includes provisions to penalize entities that facilitate sanctions evasion. Although cryptocurrencies are not explicitly mentioned, historical patterns suggest that previous sanctions have driven some transactions toward digital assets. This bill could intensify regulatory scrutiny on crypto's potential role in circumventing economic restrictions.
title: US Senate Bill Proposes 100% Tariffs on Russian Energy Buyers

details: The U.S. Treasury has announced the freezing of over $130 million in cryptocurrency wallets connected to Iran's central bank. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent stated this action is part of ongoing efforts to disrupt illicit financial activities and cut off funding channels for organizations such as the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. This comes amidst heightened tensions between the U.S. and Iran and follows the re-imposition of oil sanctions, bringing the total of Iran-linked crypto assets frozen by the U.S. to nearly $500 million.
title: US Treasury Freezes $130M in Iran-Linked Crypto Assets
